The community-area figures for Auburn Gresham give a median build year of 1949, 78.7 percent of housing built before 1970 and 38.9 percent before 1940 across 20,195 units. Those buckets stop at 1970, so nothing on this page will claim a pre-1978 percentage the source does not publish.

Owner households here number 8,722 and renter households 8,718, a 50 percent owner-occupied place. The stock behind those households is 43 percent detached, 2.8 percent attached and 54.2 percent multi-unit, at a median of 6 rooms. Median value across that stock is $196,978.

Against the other 22 Chicago community areas covered here, Auburn Gresham sits in the top four for the largest housing stock overall (20,195 units) and the largest owner-occupied market (8,722 households).

Three figures put Auburn Gresham a long way from the average of the 76 places on this site: prewar housing at 38.9 percent against a 15.8 percent average, housing in buildings of two or more at 54.2 percent against a 29 percent average and townhomes and rowhouses at 2.8 percent against a 7.5 percent average.

Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Why two houses in Auburn Gresham do not price the same

Housing with a 1949 median has been painted a lot of times, and each of those coats is now a surface the next one has to hold on to. On 6 rooms of trim that is where the hours go. Anyone who quotes Auburn Gresham interiors off a room count without asking what is already on the woodwork is guessing. With 54.2 percent of units here in buildings of two or more, a lot of the work is unit turnover and common areas rather than whole houses. That is priced per unit and scheduled around a move-out date, not around weather.

What should be on a written quote in Auburn Gresham

  • Per unit, to a date. 54.2 percent of units here are in buildings of two or more. Turnover work is priced per unit and scheduled to a move-out, not to the weather.
  • Two different customers. 50 percent owner occupancy means homeowner work and landlord work sit side by side here, and they want opposite things from a schedule.
  • Distance, stated. Auburn Gresham is 7.8 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Auburn Gresham is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Containment, not just paint. 78.7 percent of housing in Auburn Gresham was built before 1970, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is postwar masonry with a heavy share of two-flats and small apartment buildings. Trim, soffit, porches and common areas are where the exterior paint in Auburn Gresham actually is, and unit turnover sits alongside homeowner work.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1949 median build year, and the split between 43 percent detached houses, 2.8 percent attached homes and 54.2 percent in buildings of two units or more.

An inference, not a measurement. Neither the Census nor the regional housing data records what a wall in Auburn Gresham is made from, so no percentage is attached to it and none should be. Your own elevation settles it in four seconds from the sidewalk.

Pre-1978 paint is the normal case in Auburn Gresham

The community-area tables stop at 1970 and never draw a 1978 line. What they give is 78.7 percent built before 1970, which is a floor rather than an answer, and no source puts a number on the gap for Auburn Gresham. That puts most of the housing inside the federal lead-safe renovation rule, which attaches to pre-1978 homes and to work that disturbs the paint on them. In Illinois it is administered by EPA rather than by a state agency.

What it changes is the front and the back of an Auburn Gresham job, not the middle: plastic and sealed openings before, a specific cleanup standard after. It starts at roughly six square feet of disturbed paint per room inside, twenty square feet outside, and always on window replacement.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Auburn Gresham.

Ask about it early. It changes the sequence of a job rather than the price of the paint, and a contractor who has thought about it will tell you in plain terms what happens on day one.

Nothing on this page should be read as a certification claim. The slot for it below is empty because it has not been supplied, and an empty slot is more use to a homeowner in Auburn Gresham than a filled-in one nobody checked.

How quickly can somebody look at it?

Auburn Gresham is 7.8 straight-line miles from the shop, which is close enough that looking at the work and doing the work do not have to be the same trip. That matters most on small jobs, because a repair that is worth doing gets seen instead of being pushed into a bigger job later. Call 708-935-4289.

Is the $196,978 median home value in Auburn Gresham what a job here costs?

No, and the two are unrelated. $196,978 is the Census estimate of what homes in Auburn Gresham are worth, and it is on this page because the age and the size of the housing describe the work. No price for painting or remodeling appears anywhere on this site, because no local range has been established that would survive being checked. Every job is quoted after we stand in it.

Who actually shows up in Auburn Gresham?

Our crew, with Mike Walsh running it. He owns the company, and every job is quoted after we walk it. Tell us the town, the room and roughly what you want, and you will know what happens next on the same call. 708-935-4289.

Can it be done a room at a time?

Yes, and on 6-room housing it is often the right call. Doing one room properly beats doing four at a pace that shows, and it spreads the cost across seasons rather than across a credit card. Say that is what you want when you call, because it changes how the work is sequenced.
